messages:
Elena: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing an "SLA-aware residency buffer" to reduce cross-region fallbacks for short blips. Idea: reserve a tiny slice of resident-region capacity per tenant so we can absorb bursts/short outages without routing data out of region. Sketch below.
Marcus: Sounds useful. What's the cost/eviction tradeoff?
Elena: Two knobs: reserved_instances_pct (fraction of tenant qps we keep warm) and eviction_ttl_ms (how long we keep the warm allocation idle before releasing). If region goes unhealthy we free instantly. Need SRE on timing and failure modes.
Jon: From infra perspective, main pieces: routing consults buffer table, buffer allocations pinned to region (no cross-region placement), async release path, and backpressure when global capacity low. Example defaults I've prototyped: 
```yaml
residency_buffer:
  reserved_instances_pct: 0.02  # 2% of tenant concurrency
  prewarm_time_ms: 15000        # how long to prewarm before accepting live traffic
  eviction_ttl_ms: 300000       # if buffer idle this long, free it
  max_burst_ms: 30000           # max single-burst absorb time
```
Leah: Product question — can we express incremental cost? PMs will ask for per-100k reqs delta. Also want opt-in vs default behaviour documented.
Amelia: Legal note: buffer allocations must not violate data residency. Explicit requirement: buffer must always be allocated inside the tenant's resident region; no fallback proxies that move PII outside region. We need an update to the compliance checklist and KMS flow.
Marcus: Operationally, metrics we need: `cross_region_fallback_rate`, `buffer_hit_rate`, `buffer_evictions/sec`, p99 latency by route when buffer used. Alert: fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m. Also consider a circuit-breaker where repeated buffer exhaustion triggers aggressive tenant-level throttling.
Elena: Implementation detail: routing order becomes: 1) resident active capacity, 2) resident buffer, 3) fallback variants. The buffer is treated as resident capacity for policy decisions (billing/consent). If buffer is used we increment a cost bucket so biz can track.
Jon: One infra caveat — warm allocations still consume memory/KV cache if we pin them. We should avoid preloading full KV cache until buffer is actually used; keep warm as lightweight warmlapping (connection + model weights loaded but KV empty).
Leah: Agree on cost tracking. For Hosted customers maybe make this opt-in; Dedicated customers probably want it on by default for SLA.
Amelia: +1 to Dedicated default, but before turning on we need docs and a short attestation flow for customers who require in-region guarantees.
Marcus: Suggested initial thresholds: `reserved_instances_pct=0.02`, `eviction_ttl_ms=300000` (5m), `max_burst_ms=30000` (30s). We'll iterate after canary.
Elena: TL;DR decision ask — vote on three things: (a) default reserved_instances_pct=0.02, (b) eviction_ttl_ms=300000, (c) defaults: Dedicated=true, Hosted=false. Reply with :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:.
Marcus: :thumbsup: Dedicated true, Hosted false.
Leah: :thumbsup:
Jon: :thumbsup:
Amelia: :thumbsdown: need compliance doc PR before enabling for any paid tenant.
Elena: noted @Amelia — I'll open a doc PR and link KMS/residency attestations. Will also add instrumentation tasks for the metrics Marcus listed.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled to staging at 2026-04-02T18:30:00Z (11:30 PT).
Elena: Thanks all — I'll capture decisions in the RFC follow-up and file a small infra task for the async release path and light-warm strategy.
Marcus: Will add the alert and dashboard template.
Leah: I'll work the cost calc and PM blurb.
Amelia: I'll review the compliance doc PR when it's up.
